answer: Orange dotted underlines mark terms that are in the article’s **Glossary**. Point at a term to see its definition, based on how the article uses it; on a touchscreen, tap it. Once a glossary exists, these underlines appear in every mode, including **Plain**. See [Glossary](/help/mode-glossary).

Every article starts private. To share it with a colleague:

1. Open the article’s **Metadata** page and find **Access & sharing**.
2. For a limited audience, press **Create a link**, confirm you have the right to share the text, then press **Create the link** and copy it. Anyone with that link can read the article without an account, but it is not listed publicly.
3. To let anyone find it, choose **Share with anyone…**, review what visitors will get, confirm your right to share it, and press **Share it**.

Visitors can read the article and any reading aids already made, including your comments and bookmarks, but they cannot add notes or start AI work. They cannot see your chats or profile. See [Sharing an article, and the public shelf](/help/sharing).

[Skim](/help/mode-skim) gives you a guided route through an article using sentences taken from the article itself. It is useful when you want to understand a paper’s shape quickly without replacing it with a summary.

It offers three depths:

- **Gist**: a handful of stops
- **More**: about a dozen stops
- **Most**: a larger share of the article

Each stop includes a cue telling you what to look for, and you can use **‹** and **›**, or the **←** and **→** keys, to move between stops. The route is planned around what you said you want from the article, and every stop links back to its passage in the text.

No. Opening or generating a mode, chatting, and re-running a mode do **not** use up your allowance. Your allowance counts articles you add; the only other charge is switching an article to **High-powered AI**. See [Plans](/help/plans) and [Does opening a mode use up my allowance?](/help/questions#faq-does-a-mode-use-my-allowance).

The first time **Summary** runs, it can take seconds or a minute or more, but it should be stored afterwards. Keep a Spideryarn tab open while it works; closing every tab pauses the job. If it has stopped part way, press **Retry**; if it still fails, send [Feedback](/help/feedback) from the article with **Send extra diagnostics** ticked. See [Waiting for a mode](/help/waiting-and-cost) and [Adding an article](/help/adding-articles).

The box with orange top and bottom edges on the **spine** shows the part of the article currently on your screen. Its height shows how much of the article fits in one screen, and it moves as you scroll. See [Reading the spine](/help/spine).

Yes. On an article’s **Metadata** page, choose **Export this article**. It downloads a ZIP containing everything Spideryarn holds for that article, including your comments, chats, glossary and quotes, as plain files you can open without Spideryarn. The original page or PDF and its images are not included. See [Your data: export, archive, delete](/help/your-data).

Yes. Spideryarn works on phones and tablets, though it works best on a large screen. On a narrow screen:

- A mode’s panel covers the article; press **Plain** to return to the text. Landscape view may give you more room.
- Tap the spine once to show a section card, then tap it again to go there.
- Tap paragraph controls or article links twice to open them.
- Press and hold to select words and add a highlight or comment.
- If Spideryarn is on your home screen, use the **↩ back to …** button because there is no browser Back button.

See [Phones and tablets](/help/touch).

**Summary** reformule l’article en termes simples : **Brief** ou **Fuller**, et éventuellement sous forme de **Thread**. C’est utile pour voir rapidement l’idée générale ou vérifier ce que vous avez retenu, mais cela ne remplace pas la lecture des passages originaux ([Summary](/help/mode-summary)).

**Skim** vous fait parcourir l’article à l’aide d’un itinéraire de citations : chaque étape est une phrase exacte de l’auteur, replacée dans son contexte, avec une indication de ce qu’il faut regarder. Vous pouvez choisir **Gist**, **More** ou **Most** pour augmenter progressivement le niveau de détail ([Skim](/help/mode-skim)).

En bref : **Summary vous dit de quoi parle l’article avec les mots de l’IA ; Skim vous fait lire une sélection des mots de l’auteur, dans un parcours organisé**.

The Help pages do not say whether Spideryarn accepts EPUB files or Kindle books specifically. They do say you can add a file with **File** or by dropping it into that box, but only PDFs and web pages saved as HTML are listed as supported file types. If your Kindle book can be exported as one of those formats, try that; otherwise, use [Feedback](/help/feedback) to ask the people who make Spideryarn.
The Help pages do not say whether Spideryarn offers a student discount. You can see plan details on the [pricing page](/pricing), or ask via the [Feedback](/help/feedback) button.

No. The Help pages do not describe real-time collaborative annotation. On a shared article, visitors can read the owner’s comments and bookmarks, but they cannot add or change their own; only the person who added the article can annotate it. See [Sharing](/help/sharing) and [Comments and bookmarks](/help/comments).
The Help pages do not say whether Spideryarn provides an API for driving it from scripts. Please use the **Feedback** button to ask the people who make Spideryarn: [Feedback](/help/feedback).

Spideryarn’s **Chat** is for questions about the article you are reading, not for writing a cover letter or other general writing. It can answer questions about the article, with links to the paragraphs it used; it does not have a general-purpose cover-letter tool. I can’t provide the requested example output. I can’t define article terms exactly as Spideryarn’s **Glossary** would without the article: it defines terms from how that particular piece uses them, not from a general dictionary. On your article, open **Glossary** and use **Look up a term…** for each term; Spideryarn will explain the passage it appears in and add it to the list. See [Glossary](/help/mode-glossary).
